paragraphs.title: Preferring Confrontation and Criticism to Immediate Pleasure

easy.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:1 says, “A good name is better than precious ointment.”
easy.q: What is better than precious ointment?

easy.explanation: The passage says it is better to go to the house of mourning than to the house of feasting.
easy.q: Where is it better to go?

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning.”
easy.q: Where is the heart of the wise?

answers: The living will lay it to his heart
It removes the need for correction
medium.explanation: The verse says that the living will lay the experience to his heart.
medium.q: Why can the house of mourning benefit the living?

medium.explanation: Verse 5 says it is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than the song of fools.
The phrase refers to a sorrowful or serious expression through which the heart may be made better.
medium.q: What does “the sadness of the countenance” suggest in context?

challenge.explanation: The passage values mourning, correction, and reflection over passing amusement.
challenge.q: What main contrast appears in verses 1–6?

answers: It is like the crackling of thorns under a pot
challenge.explanation: The laughter of the fool is compared with a brief, noisy, and useless crackling fire.
challenge.q: Why is the fool’s laughter described as unhelpful?

answers: Pleasure is always better than correction
Correction may benefit a person more than empty entertainment
challenge.explanation: The passage prefers the rebuke of the wise to amusement that lacks lasting value.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from comparing wise rebuke with the song of fools?

paragraphs.title: Oppression, Patience, and Attention to Outcomes

easy.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:7 says, “oppression maketh a wise man mad.”
easy.q: What can oppression do to a wise man?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says that the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
easy.q: What is better than a proud spirit?

answers: That they were better than these
That they belonged to the past
easy.explanation: The passage warns against saying that the former days were better than the present ones.
easy.q: What should a person not say about former days?

answers: In the heart of the patient
medium.explanation: Verse 9 says, “anger resteth in the bosom of fools.”
medium.q: Where does anger rest according to the passage?

medium.explanation: The expression describes patience and restraint rather than pride or quick anger.
medium.q: What does “patient in spirit” mean in context?

answers: The question is not asked wisely
medium.explanation: Verse 10 says, “thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.”
medium.q: Why is asking whether former days were better considered unwise?

answers: React with anger and praise the past
Recognize oppression, practice patience, and avoid quick anger
Prefer laughter and reject all correction
challenge.explanation: The verses connect oppression and anger with a call to patience and thoughtful judgment.
challenge.q: What behavioral progression do verses 7–10 suggest?

answers: Both emphasize patience and considering the outcome
challenge.explanation: The passage values patient consideration of results over immediate emotional reaction.
challenge.q: How does “the end of a thing” relate to avoiding quick anger?

answers: It may be an unwise idealization of the past
It proves that the past was always evil
It requires anger toward the present
challenge.explanation: The writer criticizes the claim because it is not based on wise inquiry.
challenge.q: What is wrong with claiming that former days were better?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “Wisdom is good with an inheritance.”
easy.q: What does the passage say about wisdom with an inheritance?

easy.explanation: Verse 12 says that wisdom and money are both a defence.
easy.q: What do wisdom and money both provide?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “In the day of prosperity be joyful.”
easy.q: What should a person do in the day of prosperity?

answers: Wisdom gives life to those who have it
medium.explanation: Verse 12 says that the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to its possessor.
medium.q: What advantage does wisdom have over money?

answers: Pretend that there is no trouble
medium.explanation: Verse 14 says, “in the day of adversity consider.”
medium.q: What should a person do in the day of adversity?

answers: Have no connection with one another
medium.explanation: God has set prosperity and adversity in contrast with each other.
medium.q: What does “over against the other” mean in context?

answers: Money has no value at all
Both provide protection, but wisdom has an additional advantage
Wisdom and money are presented as enemies
challenge.explanation: Both are described as a defence, but wisdom also gives life.
challenge.q: What relationship between wisdom and money appears in the passage?

answers: A person must face both conditions of life
Adversity is always caused by poverty
challenge.explanation: The passage presents both prosperity and adversity as realities appointed by God.
challenge.q: What does the pairing of prosperity and adversity teach?

answers: People cannot straighten everything God has made crooked
People can repair everything with money
People cannot enjoy a prosperous day
challenge.explanation: Verse 13 asks, “who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?”
challenge.q: What human limitation is emphasized regarding God’s work?

paragraphs.title: The Proper Measure Between Righteousness and Wickedness

answers: A righteous man perishing and a wicked man living long
Every righteous person prospering and every wicked person failing
Only wise people living in the city
easy.explanation: Verse 15 describes a righteous man perishing in righteousness and a wicked man prolonging his life in wickedness.
easy.q: What did the Preacher see during the days of his vanity?

answers: Being excessively righteous or overly wise
easy.explanation: Verses 16–17 warn against being righteous or wise over much, as well as being excessively wicked or foolish.
easy.q: What does the passage warn a person against?

easy.explanation: Verse 18 says, “he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.”
easy.q: Who shall come forth from them all?

answers: So that a person does not destroy himself
So that a person can gain more money
So that a person can ignore reality
medium.explanation: Verse 16 asks, “why shouldest thou destroy thyself?”
medium.q: Why does the passage warn against excessive righteousness or wisdom?

answers: Do not go to extremes in wickedness
Practice a small amount of wickedness
Stop distinguishing between good and evil
medium.explanation: The command warns against excessive wickedness and foolishness.
medium.q: What does “be not over much wicked” mean in context?

answers: There is not a just man on earth who does good and never sins
No person can ever do good
medium.explanation: Verse 20 acknowledges that even a just person who does good still sins.
medium.q: How does the passage describe humanity generally?

answers: Moral rewards are not always obvious or immediate
There is no wisdom in the world
All wicked people are punished immediately
challenge.explanation: The righteous may perish while the wicked may prolong his life.
challenge.q: What moral problem is presented in verse 15?

answers: Moderation supported by wisdom and fear of God
challenge.explanation: The passage rejects extremes and points toward wisdom and fear of God.
challenge.q: What principle balances the warnings in this passage?

answers: It reminds us that even good people are not sinless
It claims that goodness has no value
It removes the need for wisdom
challenge.explanation: The statement limits claims of human perfection and supports humility.
challenge.q: Why is “there is not a just man upon earth” important to the warning against excessive righteousness?

paragraphs.title: Responding to Others’ Words and the Limits of Wisdom

answers: He might hear his servant curse him
easy.explanation: Verse 21 warns that listening to every word could lead a person to hear his servant curse him.
easy.q: Why should a person not take heed unto all words that are spoken?

answers: That he has also cursed others
That he has never spoken wrongly
easy.explanation: Verse 22 says that a person’s own heart knows that he has likewise cursed others.
easy.q: What does a person’s own heart know?

answers: It was found only in money
easy.explanation: He said, “I will be wise; but it was far from me.”
easy.q: What did the Preacher discover when he sought wisdom?

answers: He himself may have failed in speech
medium.explanation: The passage reminds the hearer that he has also cursed others.
medium.q: Why should a person not become immediately angry at words of cursing?

answers: It is difficult to understand fully
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the depth and difficulty of gaining complete wisdom.
medium.q: What does “exceeding deep” suggest about wisdom?

answers: Trying wisdom, claiming wisdom, and discovering that it was far away
medium.explanation: The Preacher proved things by wisdom, intended to be wise, and then found wisdom far from him.
medium.q: What sequence is described in verse 23?

answers: Recognizing personal sin and the inability to grasp everything
Believing that the speaker is perfect
Rejecting every attempt to seek wisdom
challenge.explanation: The Preacher admits his own failures and acknowledges the distance and depth of wisdom.
challenge.q: What attitude of humility appears in this passage?

answers: Both require discernment instead of automatic reaction
challenge.explanation: The passage calls for careful judgment about both other people’s words and one’s own understanding.
challenge.q: What connection exists between not listening to every word and recognizing wisdom’s limits?

answers: The difficulty of reaching complete understanding
challenge.explanation: The language reinforces the remoteness and profound depth of wisdom.
challenge.q: What does the repeated language of distance and depth emphasize?

paragraphs.title: Investigating Wickedness, the Danger of Temptation, and Human Uprightness

answers: Wisdom and the reason of things
easy.explanation: Verse 25 describes his effort to know, search, and seek out wisdom and the reason of things.
easy.q: What did the Preacher seek to know and search out?

easy.explanation: Her heart is described as snares and nets, and her hands as bands.
easy.q: How is the woman described in verse 26?

easy.explanation: Verse 29 says, “God hath made man upright.”

answers: God made man upright, but people sought many inventions
God made man wicked, but people repaired everything
There is no difference between people and their inventions
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts God’s upright creation with the many schemes devised by people.
medium.q: What contrast appears at the end of the passage?

medium.explanation: The imagery describes danger, entrapment, and temptation.
medium.q: What do “snares and nets” represent in context?

answers: One man among a thousand, but no woman among all those
medium.explanation: Verse 28 records the difficulty of finding even one person among many.
medium.q: What did the Preacher find in his search for people?

answers: The search for understanding wickedness also reveals the danger of entrapment
Temptation is presented as a path to wisdom
challenge.explanation: The Preacher examines folly and wickedness while portraying temptation as a dangerous snare.
challenge.q: What connection exists between investigating wickedness and warning about temptation?

answers: People were made upright but devised many schemes
The world was created crooked apart from humanity
challenge.explanation: The passage attributes the many inventions and schemes to humanity after God made man upright.
challenge.q: What does the conclusion teach about the source of human corruption?

answers: It emphasizes human limitation, sin, and the abundance of schemes
It proves that uprightness is unnecessary
It eliminates the possibility of wisdom
challenge.explanation: The difficult search fits the passage’s broader recognition of human weakness and wrongdoing.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the difficulty of finding a perfect person?
